rows.claim: a COMPLETED tools/call result carries a resultType marker, and its value is `complete`
rows.evidence: json_schema_2020_12_test.exs:340 — `assert result["resultType"] == "complete"` — over the result of the tools/call driven at json_schema_2020_12_test.exs:331 — `{result, log} = with_log(fn -> call("raw_extras", %{"extras" => %URI{}}) end)`. The test's call helper returns the response's result member, so an error response yields nil and an equality against a string could not hold — which is why the no-error and result-present axes are the SAME observation read at a coarser grain rather than an inference, the reading C1c-ii's two edges on this check already use. The presence axis is the one this edge is really about: it is an IN test on the key, present whatever the value, and an equality assertion against a value cannot hold unless the key is there. THE VALUE AXIS IS SILENT AND THE TWO ANTECEDENTS ARE WHY. The axis requires the resultType of an INPUT-REQUIRED response to be the input_required marker; this unit's response is a COMPLETED tools/call and carries the complete marker, so the axis's antecedent does not hold of it and the axis is not about this case. A reader who reads the axis as unconditional would call it a contradiction, and the difference is stated here so that they can.
